title: SOC-ICNN: From Polyhedral to Conic Geometry for Learning Convex Surrogate Functions
claim: A single architecture sums parallel specialized branches, each a short chain of modules, to extend a base model's expressive class.
layout: 3 stacked horizontal branches, left-to-right, merging into a sum node
description: A left-to-right block diagram. Input x on the far left splits into three horizontal lanes, each inside a dashed, color-coded rounded box. The top teal lane is the Quadratic Branch: Affine map, Squared norm, Scaling (alpha ≥ 0), and Output, a sum of squared l2 norms. The middle orange lane is the ReLU-ICNN Backbone: Hidden update, Activation, Convexity constraints, and Output. The bottom magenta lane is the Conic Branch: Affine map, Norm primitive, Scaling (lambda ≥ 0), and Output, a sum of l2 norms. Each lane is a chain of four rounded boxes with arrows between them, and each box has a title and a formula. The lane outputs join at small square junctions on a vertical line and feed a gray Σ box, which produces f_SOC(x) on the right. The eye goes first to the three colored lanes.
caption: Unified SOC-ICNN architecture. The input $\bm{x}$ is processed by three parallel branches. The quadratic branch applies an affine map followed by a squared $\ell_2$ primitive and nonnegative scaling, the ReLU-ICNN backbone captures polyhedral piecewise-linear structure under standard ICNN convexity constraints, and the conic branch applies an affine map followed by an $\ell_2$-norm primitive and nonnegative scaling. Summing the three branch outputs yields the final convex surrogate $f_{\mathrm{SOC}}(\bm{x})$, which admits an exact SOCP value-function interpretation.
abstract: Classical ReLU-based Input Convex Neural Networks (ICNNs) are equivalent to the optimal value functions of Linear Programming (LP). This intrinsic structural equivalence restricts their representational capacity to piecewise-linear polyhedral functions. To overcome this representational bottleneck, we propose the SOC-ICNN, an architecture that generalizes the underlying optimization class from LP to Second-Order Cone Programming (SOCP). By explicitly injecting positive semi-definite curvature and Euclidean norm-based conic primitives, our formulation introduces native smooth curvature into the representation while preserving a rigorous optimization-theoretic interpretation. We formally prove that SOC-ICNNs strictly expand the representational space of ReLU-ICNNs without increasing the asymptotic order of forward-pass complexity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SOC-ICNN substantially improves function approximation, while delivering competitive downstream decision quality. The code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/SOC-ICNN-4B18/.
